page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache. It supports advanced vector instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, along with hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, providing an expanded memory footprint of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local disk storage, nor does it feature bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes show that computational capabilities across general tests remain in lower percentiles. The instance recorded a single-core Geekbench score of 1135.0 and a multi-core score of 2492.0, with PassMark CPU scoring at 4320.42. Compression benchmarks demonstrate mixed behavior: single-threaded gzip compression reached an average rating of 23.92 GB/sec, whereas multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yielded 15.88 GB/sec in the lower tier. Memory tests reflect solid throughput, achieving 26.28 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and an average PassMark memory score of 2173.39.

Because the n2-highmem-4 prioritizes an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, cost efficiency is centered entirely around memory capacity rather than raw compute execution. For processing-heavy operations or large parallel builds, hardware resources are constrained by the 2 physical cores and moderate clock rates. Conversely, applications that depend on memory residency rather than extensive floating-point or vector units benefit from the generous memory footprint per core without paying for unneeded vCPUs.

The hardware profile and performance metrics indicate that the n2-highmem-4 is best configured for workloads requiring moderate processor cycles paired with significant in-memory allocation. Suitable deployments include intermediate-tier caching layers, in-memory key-value stores such as Redis, lightweight relational databases, and enterprise backends operating on moderate transactional loads.

The instance carries 33 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector extensions, but it contains no bundled GPUs or local storage. In benchmark evaluations, CPU performance falls primarily in the lower tiers, registering a multi-core Geekbench score of 2492.0, while PassMark memory and gzip compression demonstrate solid mid-range throughput.
